en.title: 8 Essential Films to Rewatch Before Cliff Booth's Further Mis-Adventures
en.summary: Dive into the gritty world of 1977 Los Angeles and Quentin Tarantino's unique storytelling before David Fincher's new film hits screens.
en.body:
## 1. Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019)
This is your absolute must-watch. It establishes the world of 1969 Hollywood, introduces us to the effortlessly cool stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt), and sets up his dynamic with actor Rick Dalton. You'll see the roots of the character and the era that will be revisited.

## 2. Pulp Fiction (1994)
Before diving into Tarantino's latest directorial effort (from his script), revisit his genre-redefining masterpiece. Its non-linear narrative, sharp dialogue, and unforgettable characters are hallmarks of his style that you'll likely find echoed in Booth's new adventure.

## 3. Reservoir Dogs (1992)
Another early Tarantino gem, this crime thriller showcases his knack for ensemble casts, tense standoffs, and intricate plotting. Understanding the foundational elements of his filmmaking will enrich your appreciation for the upcoming film's script.

## 4. Jackie Brown (1997)
This stylish crime film, based on an Elmore Leonard novel, offers a more mature Tarantino, blending character-driven drama with thrilling plot twists. Its focus on morally ambiguous characters and intricate heists provides a great thematic link.

## 5. Se7en (1995)
Since David Fincher is taking the helm for 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth', it's crucial to revisit his earlier work. This dark, gritty thriller showcases his mastery of atmosphere, suspense, and a grim vision of urban decay that might inform Booth's new setting.

## 6. Zodiac (2007)
Fincher's meticulous procedural about the hunt for the Zodiac killer is a masterclass in period detail and escalating tension. It shares a similar 1970s setting with Booth's story, highlighting Fincher's ability to immerse audiences in a specific time and place.

## 7. Fight Club (1999)
This cult classic demonstrates Fincher's ability to blend social commentary with visceral filmmaking and unexpected twists. Its exploration of identity and anti-establishment themes could resonate with the counter-culture vibe present in Tarantino's work.

## 8. The Novelization of 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth'
While not a film, the novelization is explicitly recommended to fill in pivotal backstory on Booth, including definitively answering questions about his past. Reading this offers crucial context that will pay off when watching the film, especially regarding his wife.
Bottom Line: Immerse yourself in the worlds of Tarantino and Fincher to fully appreciate Cliff Booth's latest dive into cinematic mayhem.

content_raw: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth arrives in IMAX theaters on November 25th for a two-week run, then streams on Netflix on December 23rd. Brad Pitt 's Oscar-winning stuntman Cliff Booth is back, and he has traded Tarantino's direction for David Fincher 's. Based on Tarantino's script, the story picks up in 1977, eight years after Once Upon a Time in Hollywood . It reunites Pitt and Fincher for the first time since The Curious Case of Benjamin Button in 2008, and also marks Netflix's first IMAX release.
